steps.text: In a large skillet, heat oil over medium high heat until hot. Add fillets and squeeze 1/2 of the lemon's juice over the tops. Sprinkle with pepper to taste. Cook for 4 minutes and turn. Squeeze with the remaining lemon's juice and sprinkle with pepper to taste. Continue to cook until fillets flake easily with a fork.

raw_recipe.headline: Lemon Pepper Cod
raw_recipe.description: Sauteed cod fish fillets seasoned with lemon juice and black pepper. Serve with a buttery rice pilaf and a green salad.
raw_recipe.name: Lemon Pepper Cod

review.reviewBody:
I fixed this for a husband who LOVES fish and two 8-year old picky eaters. There
were no leftovers! I served it with yellow rice and mixed vegetables. The whole 
meal was done and on the table in less than 30 minutes. At last, a great fish dish
that does not require dredging and deep frying fish. I just wish I could give it
more than a five card rating!
I rubbed the fish with EVOO and then coated with lemon pepper seasoning. Was not bland at all this way. Oh, and I baked it - 400 for 10 mins. Kids loved it (of course they though it was chicken)!
This was great fish. I didn't not have a lemon so I used lemon juice. I distributed 1 tbsp per piece of fish on each side. I also used olive oil instead of vegetable. Will definitely make again.

I've made this twice in the last week. First time was as written, got rave reviews. The second time I used butter instead of oil, got even more raves. This dish is what I call 'stupid simple', and results in perfectly cooked, beautifully seasoned fish. DH wants it in my regular rotation. Great recipe!

This recipe was good and easy. I added white wine to deglaze the pan and before adding any lemon juice. To thicken the resulting sauce I added about 1 tbsp of butter and added dried parsley. Served it with Peas and Pancetta from this site and added a spoon or two of the sauce on top. It was very good and satisfying dinner. I will make it again with my addition.
5 for ease, 1 for (lack of) flavor. Definitely add SALT.

Super easy and delicious, and works perfectly with any mild fish. I usually marinate the fish in lemon juice for about an hour for a little more flavor. It also doesn't hurt to top it with a bread crumb/Parmesan mixture then broil for a couple of minutes. Thanks!

A tasty, basic recipe that doesn’t cover up cod’s naturallysweet, buttery flavor. It is lacking salt though, so I would definitely add a sprinkle, and I found the cook time to be too long for the thickness of my cod pieces (about ¾” thick). You could also get away with using less oil than called for. I would also add the lemon juice after searing, otherwise it tends to 'steam' the first and makes it difficult to get a good sear. I served this with roasted veggies and rice.

I'm sure I'll make this again because it's so simple, and the taste is so simple my picky 7 year-old ate it. It is somewhat bland, so I added a sprinkle of dried dill to it. --update-- I make this a lot with both cod and tilapia. It's quick and tasty. I now use 1 T butter and 1 T veg oil. If I don't have lemon juice, I sprinkle on lemon pepper instead. It's great served with a pasta side dish and a veggie.

Love this simple recipe! I actually used flounder. Only difference is I added pepper to a tbs of flour, placed seasoned flour in plastic bag and then shook the flounder to lightly coat the fish. Then, placed 1 tbs of butter in skillet, melted it, added fish and squeezed the lemon on top. OOH! SO GOOD! Someone mentioned adding garlic. I might try that next.

This recipe looked perfect. Unfortunately I was in a hurry by the time I goofed around and read awhile and by that time I needed to eat right away! I preheated the oven to 375° F. Put cod (any fish will do) in pan that had been generously sprayed with regular Pam, seasoned fish with salt, pepper and lemon pepper then sprayed with Butter Pam and put in oven. When fish looked slightly brown on top, removed it, flipped fish and repeated seasoning. Put back in the oven and when the cod smelled extra good I took it out and ate nearly 5 ounces right out of the pan before I even got a side dish going! I’ll do this again when I get in a pinch and will definitely try the above recipe too!
Tasty and simple to make. Like others suggested, add some salt.
The cod was very flavorful with the juice of a whole lemon and pepper. Cooked it for 4 minutes on each side in olive oil and added capers in the pan right before serving.
This was great, and easy to make. I used lemon pepper to season, and cooked it in olive oil. Definitely a "Make it again meal"
I made this following the recipe to a T. This was very disappointing as it lacked flavor. The only thing that was good about it was that was easy and quick, then again so is a boiled hot dog.
Husband said he likes cod better this way than in the oven. Easy, healthy, and he likes it equals 5+stars! Thanks!
Simple and straight forward, very easy and good.
I was looking for a low fat recipe and this is it. Tasty but plain. I paired it with homemade tartar sauce and it was yummy.

it was good! Tho' hubby and I both felt it could use just a tad more flavor. Next time I will try with garlic simmering in the oil and maybe add a little Old Bay Seasoning... being careful NOT to overpower the buttery flavor of the Cod. Thanks for the good, easy recipe.
